match.reason: The bank point covers the historical shift in Australia's trading partners and names China as largest partner, but it does not teach that Asia buys most of Australia's exports, the export commodities (iron ore, coal, gas, education), or India as a partner, so it is related rather than the same idea, and it is pitched at Year 12 depth.

note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, other: The clue lists China, Japan, South Korea and India and asks where they are, which all but hands over the answer 'Asia'. A student needs only basic geography, not the idea from the card.

rejected.title: Australia's trade with Asia
card: Asia is the region that buys most of Australia's exports. This makes Asia Australia's most important group of trading partners.
Many of the exports are minerals and energy, such as iron ore, coal and gas. These are used in Asian factories, power stations and steel making.
Education is also an export. When students from Asia pay fees to study in Australia, Australia earns income from another country.
China, Japan, South Korea and India are major partners. Each buys large amounts of Australian goods and services.
rejected.remember: Asia buys most of Australia's exports, from iron ore, coal and gas to education.

a.q: Which region buys the largest share of Australia's exports?
opts: Asia
Europe
North America
Africa
a.why: Asia buys most of Australia's exports, including iron ore, coal, gas and education. Europe is a trading partner, but it buys a smaller share than Asia.
a.clue: Think of where China, Japan, South Korea and India are.

b.q: Priya from India pays fees to study at a university in Adelaide. How does this link to Australia's trade with Asia?
opts: It is an Australian export of education to Asia
It is an Australian import of education from Asia
It is an Australian export of minerals to Asia
It is an Indian export of education to Australia
b.why: Priya pays an Australian university, so Australia is the seller and earns income from another country. That makes it an Australian export of education, not an import or an Indian export. It counts as an export wherever the student comes from.
b.clue: Who is selling the education, and who is paying?

problems.detail: The explanation for (b) ends 'India is a major partner, so the trade counts.' This wrongly suggests a sale only counts as an export when the buyer is a major partner. Education sold to a student from any country is an export. Better: 'It counts as an export wherever the student comes from.'

a.q: Which statement best describes where Australia's exports go and what they are?
opts: Most go to Asia, including services like education
Most go to North America, mainly as farm goods
Most go to Asia, but they are all goods, not services
